verdict.rationale: The evidence shows several bulk-style capabilities: one MCP prompt can check read status across many emails, draft all the nudges, and schedule their sends; Auto Archive and Auto Labels act automatically on whole classes of mail; and split inbox lets users work through emails of the same type together. However, none of it explicitly documents user-driven bulk actions such as multi-select archive, label, or delete on a chosen set of items, and MCP sends need per-send approval. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of multi-select/bulk actions on arbitrary item sets, bulk operations via prompt beyond follow-ups, and independent hands-on corroboration.
